brief.headline: Tajuana fell at home on 2026-10-02 and now needs moderate help with bathing and lower-body dressing. Her son and caregiver, Robert, reports exhaustion and has asked for respite.

items.statement: Tajuana fell in the bathroom at night on 2026-10-02 and was found on the floor by her son. She denied head strike or loss of consciousness. She had a small left forearm skin tear, and fall risk was reassessed as high. PT referral was placed.
items.verifier_note: All details match the 2026-10-02 nursing note.

items.statement: PT evaluation on 2026-10-06 found slow, unsteady gait with intermittent cane use and a Timed Up and Go of 19 seconds. PT recommended a front-wheeled walker, a home safety evaluation, and bathroom grab bars. PT will see her twice weekly.
items.verifier_note: The PT note matches on gait, TUG, recommendations, and twice-weekly visits.

items.statement: OT reassessment on 2026-11-05 found she now needs moderate assistance with bathing and lower-body dressing. She was independent at the last review. OT recommends a tub transfer bench, a handheld shower, and more home care hours for bathing. On 2026-11-01 the aide gave hands-on help getting out of the tub, and she said she has been skipping showers because she fears slipping.
items.verifier_note: The OT note and aide note support every detail, including the prior independence.

items.statement: On 2026-10-11 her son Robert, the primary caregiver, reported exhaustion and poor sleep. He is worried about managing evenings alone and requested respite. Respite options and a caregiver support group were discussed.
items.verifier_note: The social work note matches on all details.

items.statement: She went to the partner hospital ED on 2026-09-18 for a urinary tract infection with acute confusion. She was treated and released the same day on nitrofurantoin 100 MG, with a course that ran 2026-09-18 to 2026-09-23. At the 2026-09-21 PCP follow-up she was back to baseline per her son, and the PCP planned close monitoring for two weeks.
items.verifier_note: The ED visit, nitrofurantoin 100 MG, the 09-18 to 09-23 course dates, and the PCP follow-up are supported. The PCP note says only that it will monitor closely over the next two weeks. The statement adds 'planned close monitoring for two weeks', which is close but is not a significant mismatch. Taken as a whole it is supported, but the 7-day follow-up instruction is not mentioned. The 09-23 end date is also consistent with 5 days of treatment. The one discrepancy is the PCP follow-up date: the note is dated 2026-09-21, which is within 7 days. Verdict is therefore generous, but strictly all facts are present.

items.statement: She is skipping showers because she fears slipping (2026-11-01). This is a hygiene concern and may reflect fear of falling after the 2026-10-02 fall.
items.verifier_note: The skipped showers from fear of slipping are supported. The link to fear of falling after the 10-02 fall is a hedged inference ('may reflect'), and calling it a hygiene concern is an interpretation. The notes do not state either.

items.statement: No influenza vaccine is recorded for the current season, which began 2026-08-01. Her last flu vaccine was 2025-12-16.
items.verifier_note: The immunization record shows no flu vaccine this season, a season start of 2026-08-01, and a last vaccine on 2025-12-16.

checks: Confirm the review window (2026-09-01 to 2026-11-30) and pull all encounters, ED visits, urgent care visits, and hospital admissions/discharges in that window, including any readmissions.

Falls and near-falls review: count, circumstances, injuries, and whether a post-fall assessment was done. Participant has chronic paralysis (spinal cord lesion), so check transfer and wheelchair-related incidents and skin injuries.

Anticoagulation and bleeding safety: warfarin is active alongside clopidogrel. Check INR results and monitoring dates in the window, any out-of-range values, dose changes, and any bleeding, bruising, GI bleed, or hematuria events. Also check the anemia trend (hemoglobin/hematocrit) given the concurrent anemia diagnosis.

Medication changes since last review: list all starts and stops. Specifically check the antihypertensive set (amlodipine 2.5 mg, HCTZ 25 mg, lisinopril 10 mg, metoprolol succinate 100 mg) for recent additions, dose changes, or duplicate or missing fills, and verify the start dates shown (several 2025-12-16) against the prior review.

Blood pressure and heart rate trend across the window, including orthostatic readings if recorded, given multiple antihypertensives, paralysis, and aortic stenosis. Flag any hypotension, bradycardia, or readings above the team's thresholds. Check for chest pain and nitroglycerin use (ischemic heart disease).

Diabetes and metabolic monitoring: HbA1c and glucose values in the window, hypoglycemia events, whether a diabetes medication is on the active list (none currently is; confirm whether this is intentional), statin status (simvastatin 20 mg) and lipid results given hypertriglyceridemia, and foot or neuropathy checks.

Recurrent UTI: count symptomatic episodes, urine cultures and results, antibiotic courses started or completed in the window, and any related ED visits or delirium. Review catheter or bladder management documentation and check hydration and fluid intake.

Weight and nutrition trend: compare current weight and BMI against the prior review, flag change of 5% or more over the window, and check intake and any dietitian referral, given obesity and diabetes.

Pain and function: review pain scores and analgesic use (acetaminophen, topical hydrocortisone) for chronic low back pain and fibromyalgia. Check ADL and mobility scores, transfer status, wheelchair or equipment condition, and any new functional decline.

Cognition, mood, and engagement: screen results (e.g., PHQ or GDS, cognitive screen), delirium signs, attendance at programs and day services, social isolation indicators, and any new behavioral concerns. Confirm the allergy record is complete, since the reaction field is blank.

Caregiver situation and care-plan items due: confirm caregiver availability and strain, any changes in living situation, due dates for care-plan goals, pending referrals, advance directive or code status review, vaccination status, and the next scheduled review. Flag items overdue as of 2026-11-30.
